entities.name: Ivan Yevreinov
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ivan Mikhaylovich Yevreinov (1724-02-03) was a prominent Russian geodesist and explorer who mapped the vast territories of Siberia.

As a member of the 1732-1743 expedition to the Amur River, led by Mikhail Gvozdev, Ivan Yevreinov played a crucial role in charting the region's geography, collecting data on its flora and fauna, and establishing trade relationships with local indigenous populations.

His work laid the groundwork for future Russian expansion into Siberia, contributing significantly to the country's growth as an empire.

The legacy of Ivan Yevreinov extends beyond his scientific discoveries, influencing the development of cartography and exploration in 18th-century Russia. His expeditions also had a lasting impact on the indigenous peoples of the region, shaping their interactions with European colonizers for centuries to come.

"We must map the world to truly know it," Ivan Yevreinov once said, echoing the sentiments of many geographers and explorers of his time.
